claims.text: CrFeCoNiX alloys can be prepared as single-phase or controlled multiphase solid solutions by mechanical alloying followed by annealing.
The proposed comparison exposes CrFeCoNiX alloys for approximately 72 hours at or above 900 °C in a controlled oxidative or mildly corrosive atmosphere.
CrFeCoNi without Si, Mn, or Al is the baseline comparator under identical exposure conditions.
During high-temperature exposure, the reactive element X selectively oxidizes.
Selective oxidation of X can produce a protective oxide scale.
Oxide/alloy interfacial coherency is determined primarily by crystallographic lattice mismatch and coherency strain.
A close crystallographic match between the oxide and substrate promotes oxide-scale adherence.
A close crystallographic match between the oxide and substrate causes the scale to grow more slowly.
A close match in thermal expansion between scale and substrate reduces interfacial stress, cracking, and spallation.
Oxide growth kinetics influence stress accumulation, cracking, and spallation.
Grain-boundary density controls oxide growth kinetics and the distribution of stress.
Controlled grain-boundary characteristics facilitate stress relaxation and limit oxygen ingress at critical sites.
Poor lattice matching accelerates oxide growth.
Poor lattice matching amplifies stress concentrations and thereby promotes cracking or spallation.
Al additions can form a protective alumina scale that grows more slowly and is more stable than chromia at high temperature.
Al-derived alpha-alumina has good lattice matching with the CrFeCoNiAl substrate.
CrFeCoNiAl will exhibit a slower-growing, more uniform, and less cracked scale than baseline CrFeCoNi.
Oxides derived from Si or Mn will have greater lattice mismatch than the Al-derived oxide and will show faster growth, microcracking, and spallation.
Phase distributions and local compositional inhomogeneities can introduce variability in oxide-scale structure and long-term performance.

The mechanism would be falsified if a nominally low-mismatch alloy with beneficial microstructure shows rapid growth and extensive cracking or spallation indistinguishable from the baseline or high-mismatch alloys.
